title: Python SDK: streaming surface - mini-batch ACK/NACK and resume flow
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: SDK consumers are asking for a small, predictable buffering primitive for chat streaming that allows application-level ACK/NACK semantics (to indicate downstream persistence or rejection), low-latency delivery for small responses, and a resumable resume/seek surface that is simple to adopt. Current iterator and event-adapter designs are flexible but either too heavy (full checkpoint DSL) or too opinionated (automatic checkpointing without app visibility).

Proposal: Add a lightweight MiniBatchConsumer API on top of the existing streaming primitives. Core ideas:
- Mini-batches collect 1..N fragments (configurable N and timeout) and deliver a single 'batch event' to the consumer. Batches can be acknowledged (ACK) or negatively acknowledged (NACK).
- ACK signals success and advances an internal per-session cursor. NACK triggers a retry policy that can: immediate re-enqueue, escalate to manual inspection, or fast-fail depending on NACK reason.
- Resume surface: the consumer can request resume(token) where token is an opaque string produced by the runtime representing last-ACKed position. Token is safe for short-term retention and can be persisted to user storage.
- Backpressure: consumer exposes a simple .pause()/.resume() surface; internal buffer size and mini-batch timeout enforce SLOs.
- Observability: each batch event emits structured telemetry tags (session_id, batch_size, latency_ms, ack_status). SDK emits counter/metric hooks and optional span annotations.

Why this is different: reduces cognitive load vs full checkpoint DSL; provides clear app-level contract (ACK/NACK) useful for downstream persistence (DB writes, analytics). Works for both short and long responses and intentionally minimizes API surface so we can iterate quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Add MiniBatchConsumer class to python-sdk with configuration: max_batch_size:int, batch_timeout_ms:int, buffer_limit:int.
SDK surface supports ack(batch_token) and nack(batch_token, reason:str) with documented retry policies.
Resume(token) successfully reconnects to a stream and delivers fragments after the token position (best-effort, documented semantics).
Backpressure pause()/resume() prevents memory growth under sustained load and surface documented behavior when buffer_limit exceeded.
Emit telemetry events for batch delivery/ack/nack with tags documented in the SDK reference.
Include two end-to-end examples in the repo: (1) DB write with ACK-on-commit; (2) idempotent consumer that NACKs on schema mismatch and escalates to retry queue.
Unit/integration tests covering ACK happy path, NACK -> retry backoff, resume after disconnect, and pause/resume under load.
implementation_notes: High-level implementation: wrap existing stream iterator with a small stateful adapter that accumulates fragments into a batch buffer. Deliver a BatchEvent object (simple dataclass) that contains fragments:list[str], batch_token:str, metadata:dict (session_id, sequence_range).

batch_token should be opaque (base64 of session+seq) and short-lived. Avoid exposing internal offsets semantics. Document that token can be persisted for short-term checkpoints but may expire across model rollouts.
Retry semantics: default policy = 3 immediate retries (fast retry), then exponential backoff up to 30s, then escalate to on_error hook. Allow override via MiniBatchConsumer(retry_policy=..).
Edge cases: large single-fragment messages bigger than max_batch_size should be always delivered as single-batch with a size warning telemetry tag.

Concurrency: implementation will utilize asyncio.Queue with configurable maxsize. pause() sets an internal paused flag and stops pulling from upstream stream; resume() restarts. Ensure shutdown drains outstanding ACKs before closing.

Telemetry: integrate with existing telemetry client (redwood.telemetry). Emit counters: batch_delivered, batch_ack, batch_nack, batch_retry. Emit histogram for batch_delivery_latency_ms and gauge for buffer_occupancy.
Public docs: short migration guide comparing MiniBatchConsumer to existing streaming iterator patterns and recommended usage patterns for small vs large workloads.
Compatibility: ensure the adapter works with existing server-side streaming endpoints without protocol change (server continues to emit chunked events). The adapter operates client-side only.
risks: Users may misuse tokens as durable checkpoints; need clear docs and error messages if token is stale or missing.
If consumers block ACK path for long periods, buffer could fill; ensure default buffer_limit is conservative and clear failure mode is documented.
Complex retry policies may interact poorly with downstream idempotency; include example patterns for idempotent commit tokens.
testing_plan: Unit tests for batching logic: boundary conditions (1, N-1, N), timeout firing, oversized fragment handling.
Simulated network tests: inject disconnects and ensure resume(token) resumes from last-ACKed position when server supports resume, otherwise documents best-effort semantics.
Load test: run mini-batch consumer under steady 200 rps of small fragments and verify memory usage and telemetry values remain within target SLOs.
Chaos test: NACK cascade scenario to validate retry backoff and on_error escalation path.
